$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. The known USB radio dongles of OneMind OS (issue #732). One table, read three ways: Go renders the image's udev rules from it (internal/detect/radios.go -> os/rootfs/layers/onemind/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/70-onemind-radio.rules) and checks each named radio against it, and the gateway labels the radio-found cards (core/onemind_core/radios.py, GET /v1/radios). A known dongle gets the stable name /dev/onemind/<kind><n> (n = the lowest free number for that kind, so the first LoRa radio is lora0) and group onemind-radio. match=product: the USB vendor and product id AND the USB product string (a lowercase glob over the lowercased string) identify the product, because cheap USB-serial chips share one id across many products. match=id: only the id is known and it belongs to a generic USB-serial chip, so the radio is named but its card says the id alone proves nothing. A kind listed under confirm needs the owner to confirm the radio (and its firmware) on its card before anything may open it; OneMind never probes a device. A USB serial line that matches no row is listed but never named and never granted. A new row is a contract change: add it here with its source, then run go test ./internal/detect -run TestRadioUdevRules -update.
name: /dev/onemind/{kind}{n}

kinds.zigbee-thread: an IEEE 802.15.4 radio that runs Zigbee or Thread firmware, one at a time; the USB ids do not say which
kinds.lora: a LoRa radio on a USB serial line

devices.model: SONOFF Zigbee 3.0 USB Dongle Plus V2
